stem: Maria R. (retail SMB owner) just said: "Yeah, that does sound interesting. Send me something?" You have Calendar open in a second window. Which close sets Next_Step_Booked__c = TRUE in Salesforce during this call?

options.label: A
options.text: "I'll send a calendar invite by email later today."
options.rationale: Partly right. The flag won't change until you send the invite, and "later today" is where the deal slips. Top reps send during the call.

options.label: B
options.text: "What's the best 20 minutes next week to walk you through the SMB version — Tuesday 11 or Thursday 2?"
options.rationale: Yes. Two specific slots in one sentence, sent during the call. This is M.G.'s close, and the Salesforce flag changes before you hang up.

options.label: C
options.text: "Let me know which day works best for you."
options.rationale: An open-ended close. It puts the work on the buyer and gives no two slots to choose from.

options.label: D
options.text: "I'll follow up next week with some options."
options.rationale: "Follow up" is where these deals were lost. None of the buyers in the sample calls re-engaged.

stem: A peer rep tells you: "I always pick the slots after the call ends — I want to double-check my own calendar first." What does that habit cost, going by the Gong and Salesforce data?

options.label: A
options.text: Nothing. The buyer accepted, so the booking is the same.
options.rationale: No. The booking may still happen, but the Next_Step_Booked__c flag stays FALSE on the day of the call, and buyers re-engage about as rarely as they do after "I'll follow up".

options.label: B
options.text: The Salesforce flag stays FALSE that day, and buyers re-engage about as rarely as after "I'll follow up".
options.rationale: Yes. "After the call" is the same mistake under another name. The flag has two states: set during the call, or not set.

options.label: C
options.text: It is fine if the rep sends the invite within 24 hours.
options.rationale: Not according to the Gong sample. In one recorded call the rep sent the invite the next morning, and the buyer never re-engaged.

options.label: D
options.text: It is better. Checking the calendar twice prevents double-booking.
options.rationale: You can fix a calendar clash by sending a new invite. You can't fix a buyer who has gone cold, so the second cost is far bigger.

stem: You read out two slots, the buyer says "Tuesday 11 works." What is the very next thing you do, still on the call?

options.label: A
options.text: Thank them and end the call. Confirm by email tomorrow.
options.rationale: A mistake. Confirm now: the buyer's yes is your cue to send the invite, not to wait.

options.label: B
options.text: Click "Send invite" in Calendar and watch Next_Step_Booked__c flip to TRUE in Salesforce.
options.rationale: Yes. Send the invite, check that the flag changes, then confirm with the buyer that the invite is in their inbox. Do all three before you hang up.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask whether they want a reminder 1 day before.
options.rationale: A reminder is a nice extra. Sending during the call is not optional, and it comes first.

options.label: D
options.text: Pivot to a second pitch prop while you have their attention.
options.rationale: Tempting, but you risk losing the booking. Lock the next step first, then pitch on the booked call.
